senses.gloss: The event or remark that sets off something much bigger.
examples: The arrest was the *spark* that set off weeks of protests.
One careless comment was the *spark* for the whole argument.
Cheap credit provided the *spark* for the housing boom.

senses.gloss: A small trace of a feeling, quality, or energy.
examples: There was still a *spark* of hope in her voice.
The team played without a *spark* of energy.
I saw a *spark* of interest when I mentioned the job.

senses.gloss: A long thin piece of a vegetable, either a whole shoot or a lengthwise slice.
examples: Steam the asparagus *spears* for about four minutes.
She packed a pickle *spear* next to the sandwich.
Serve the broccoli *spears* with a squeeze of lemon.

senses.gloss: A television program made as a single show outside the regular schedule.
examples: The network aired a two-hour holiday *special*.
Her stand-up *special* comes out next month.
We watch the same Christmas *special* every year.

senses.gloss: A period of time, especially one of particular weather or a brief bout of illness.
examples: We had a dry *spell* that lasted all of July.
She had a dizzy *spell* and had to sit down.
He worked at the paper for a *spell* after college.

senses.gloss: An area of activity, knowledge, or influence.
examples: In the political *sphere*, nothing moves quickly.
The two powers divided the region into *spheres* of influence.
She is well known in the *sphere* of medical research.

senses.gloss: A sudden sharp increase in a number or level.
examples: The city saw a *spike* in emergency calls during the heat wave.
There was a brief *spike* in gas prices last spring.
Doctors reported a *spike* in flu cases in January.

senses.gloss: A long thick pointed piece of metal or wood.
examples: The fence around the yard is topped with iron *spikes*.
He drove a *spike* into the railroad tie.
Steel *spikes* held the tent lines to the ground.

senses.gloss: The stiff back edge of a book, where the pages are joined.
examples: The title was printed down the *spine* in gold.
The *spine* of my old dictionary is cracked.
She read the *spines* until she found the cookbook.

senses.gloss: A sharp needle-like point on a plant or an animal.
examples: The cactus is covered in fine white *spines*.
A porcupine raises its *spines* when it feels threatened.
Watch out for the *spines* when you clean that fish.

senses.gloss: A steady uncontrolled rise or fall that keeps feeding itself.
examples: The company went into a financial *spiral* after the recall.
Losing the job started a downward *spiral*.
Officials worried about an inflationary *spiral*.

senses.gloss: A long metal rod that meat is turned on over a fire.
examples: A whole pig was turning slowly on the *spit*.
He basted the chicken as it rotated on the *spit*.
The restaurant roasts lamb on an open *spit*.

senses.gloss: A raised part fitted to a car or an airplane wing to control airflow.
examples: The car came with a rear *spoiler*.
The pilot raised the *spoilers* as the plane touched down.
He added a *spoiler* and new wheels to the old Mustang.

senses.gloss: A person judged by how well they take teasing, losing, or a joke.
senses.ru: человек, умеющий держаться (в игре, при поражении)
examples: Be a good *sport* and let your sister go first.
He was a good *sport* about the whole prank.
She's a terrible *sport* when she loses at cards.

senses.gloss: A particular place or area.
examples: This is a good *spot* for a picnic.
I found a parking *spot* right in front.
We picked a shady *spot* under the trees.

senses.gloss: A position in a group, a list, or a schedule.
examples: She earned a *spot* on the varsity team.
The song held the top *spot* for six weeks.
There's one *spot* left in the morning class.

senses.gloss: A short advertisement on television or radio.
examples: The company bought a thirty-second *spot* during the game.
They filmed three *spots* for the new campaign.
Radio *spots* cost a lot less than television.

senses.gloss: Very fine drops of water blown or thrown through the air.
examples: *Spray* from the waterfall soaked our jackets.
Salt *spray* had rusted the railings.
The wind picked up and sent *spray* over the bow.

senses.gloss: A small arrangement of cut flowers or leafy branches.
examples: She carried a *spray* of white roses.
A *spray* of lilies lay on the casket.
He tucked a *spray* of baby's breath into the vase.

senses.gloss: A soft food that is put on bread or crackers.
examples: Try the olive *spread* on the toast.
I bought a cheese *spread* for the crackers.
This *spread* has less fat than butter.

senses.gloss: A large amount of food laid out for guests.
examples: They put out quite a *spread* for the holidays.
The hotel offers a breakfast *spread* every morning.
Her mother laid out a *spread* that fed twenty people.

senses.gloss: Something that encourages an action or speeds up a development.
examples: Tax breaks acted as a *spur* to new building.
The award was a *spur* to keep writing.
We bought the tickets on the *spur* of the moment.

senses.gloss: An indoor game in which two players hit a small rubber ball against the walls of a court.
examples: They play *squash* every Tuesday at the gym.
He hurt his shoulder during a game of *squash*.
The club has four *squash* courts in the basement.

senses.gloss: A sudden sharp feeling of pain or emotion.
examples: She felt a *stab* of pain in her side.
A *stab* of guilt hit him when he read the letter.
There was a *stab* of jealousy in his voice.

senses.gloss: A group of racehorses, athletes, or performers managed by one owner or company.
examples: The trainer keeps a *stable* of twenty horses.
The agency has a *stable* of young writers.
He fought for the same *stable* his whole career.

senses.gloss: A colored liquid brushed onto wood to darken it while letting the grain show.
examples: We put two coats of *stain* on the deck.
This *stain* gives pine the color of walnut.
He wiped the extra *stain* off with a rag.

senses.gloss: A mark of shame on someone's name or record.
examples: The scandal left a *stain* on his reputation.
The verdict removed the *stain* from her record.
Corruption remains a *stain* on the department.

senses.gloss: A tool for pressing a design onto a surface, or the mark it leaves.
examples: The clerk put a *stamp* in my passport.
She keeps a rubber *stamp* with the return address on it.
The document still needs the notary's *stamp*.

senses.gloss: A frame or base made to hold something up.
examples: Put the sheet music on the *stand*.
The TV sits on a low metal *stand*.
He bought a *stand* for his new guitar.

senses.gloss: The rows of seats where people watch a game, usually in the plural.
examples: The *stands* were packed for the final.
Her parents cheered from the *stands*.
We sat high in the *stands* behind home plate.

senses.gloss: The place in a courtroom where a witness sits to give evidence.
examples: The officer took the *stand* on Thursday morning.
She was visibly nervous on the *stand*.
The defense called three witnesses to the *stand*.

senses.gloss: A famous and successful performer or athlete.
examples: He became a *star* after his first album.
The movie *stars* arrived in dark glasses.
She was the *star* of the school play.

senses.gloss: A pointed shape used as a symbol, a reward, or a rating.
examples: The teacher put a gold *star* on her paper.
The restaurant earned three *stars* in the guide.
Draw a *star* at the top of the tree.

senses.gloss: The carbohydrate found in foods like potatoes, rice, and bread.
examples: Potatoes are high in *starch*.
Cut back on *starches* if you want to lose weight.
Rinse the rice to wash off the extra *starch*.

senses.gloss: A sudden jerk of the body caused by surprise or fright.
examples: He woke with a *start* when the phone rang.
That noise gave me quite a *start*.
She sat up with a *start* and looked at the clock.

senses.gloss: A player who is in the lineup when a game begins.
examples: He's been a *starter* since his sophomore year.
Two *starters* were out with injuries.
The coach named tonight's *starter* after practice.

senses.gloss: A mixture of flour and water kept alive to make bread rise.
examples: She feeds her sourdough *starter* every morning.
The *starter* has to bubble before you use it.
He gave me a jar of *starter* from his own batch.

senses.gloss: The condition that someone or something is in at a particular time.
examples: He was in a *state* of shock for days.
The president spoke about the *state* of the economy.
She was in no *state* to drive home.

senses.gloss: The electrical charge that builds up on hair, clothes, or carpet.
examples: The dry air gives my hair *static*.
I got a shock of *static* off the doorknob.
Dryer sheets cut down on *static*.

senses.gloss: The importance or respect a person or institution has earned.
examples: She is a scientist of international *stature*.
The prize raised his *stature* in the field.
The paper has lost *stature* over the years.

senses.gloss: A pot or basket with holes, used to cook food over boiling water.
examples: Put the broccoli in the *steamer* for five minutes.
We got a bamboo *steamer* for dumplings.
The rice cooker came with a *steamer* tray.

senses.gloss: A single movement made by lifting a foot and putting it down.
examples: Take two *steps* to your left.
The baby took her first *steps* last week.
He was only a few *steps* behind me.

senses.gloss: One action or stage in a process.
examples: The first *step* is to gather your documents.
Follow the *steps* in the order they are listed.
Filing the report was an important *step* forward.

senses.gloss: The tip at the center of a flower, where pollen lands.
examples: Pollen sticks to the *stigma* and fertilizes the flower.
Saffron is made from the dried *stigmas* of a crocus.
Draw an arrow from the anther to the *stigma*.

senses.gloss: A secret police operation set up to catch someone breaking the law.
examples: Detectives arrested six people in the *sting*.
The *sting* was run out of a rented storefront.
Federal agents set up a *sting* to catch the dealers.

senses.gloss: An act of mixing something with a spoon or a stick.
examples: Give the soup a *stir* before you serve it.
The sauce needs a *stir* every few minutes.
A quick *stir* will keep the rice from sticking.

senses.gloss: The supply of goods a store has on hand.
examples: That size is out of *stock*.
We keep extra batteries in *stock*.
The *stock* in the back room is running low.

senses.gloss: A liquid made by boiling bones or vegetables, used as a base for soups and sauces.
examples: Add two cups of chicken *stock*.
She freezes the *stock* in ice cube trays.
Homemade *stock* makes a real difference in the soup.

senses.gloss: A supply of something kept for future use.
examples: Squirrels build up a *store* of nuts for winter.
The town keeps a *store* of salt for icy roads.
She has a deep *store* of patience.

senses.gloss: A sudden violent outburst of public feeling or trouble.
examples: The remark set off a *storm* of criticism.
The bill passed after a political *storm*.
Her resignation caused a media *storm*.

senses.gloss: An account of events, real or invented, told to entertain or inform.
examples: Grandpa told us ghost *stories* on the porch.
It's a *story* about two brothers in Ohio.
She never got to finish the *story*.

senses.gloss: A report in a newspaper or on a news program.
examples: The *story* ran on the front page.
A reporter has been working on the *story* for months.
That *story* has been all over the news.

senses.gloss: Pressure or worry that is hard to bear, or the force pulling on something.
examples: The long hours put a *strain* on their marriage.
The heat wave put a *strain* on the power grid.
You can hear the *strain* in his voice.

senses.gloss: A particular type of a virus, bacterium, or plant.
examples: A new *strain* of flu is going around.
Farmers planted a *strain* of wheat that resists drought.
The lab identified two *strains* of the bacteria.

senses.gloss: An unbroken run of wins, losses, or luck.
examples: The team is on a six-game winning *streak*.
His hot *streak* ended in April.
She hit a losing *streak* and stopped playing.

senses.gloss: A noticeable part of someone's character.
examples: He has a stubborn *streak*.
There's a mean *streak* in that dog.
She has a romantic *streak* under all that logic.

senses.gloss: A steady flow of people, vehicles, or things.
examples: A steady *stream* of customers came through the door.
There was an endless *stream* of cars on the highway.
The office got a *stream* of complaints all week.

senses.gloss: A live video or audio broadcast sent over the internet.
examples: Thousands watched the *stream* of the concert.
The *stream* kept freezing during the game.
He starts his *stream* around eight every night.

senses.gloss: A clear step forward in progress, usually used in the plural.
examples: The company has made great *strides* in safety.
Medicine has made huge *strides* since then.
She made real *strides* with her English this year.

senses.gloss: A military attack, especially one from the air.
examples: The air *strike* hit a supply depot.
Two *strikes* were reported overnight.
The general ordered a *strike* at dawn.

senses.gloss: In baseball, a pitch that counts against the batter.
examples: That's *strike* two.
He went down on three straight *strikes*.
The umpire called it a *strike* and the crowd booed.

senses.gloss: A worker who has stopped working as part of a labor protest.
examples: *Strikers* gathered outside the plant gate.
The company met with the *strikers* on Friday.
Police kept the *strikers* off the road.

senses.gloss: A single movement of a brush, a pen, or a hand across a surface.
examples: He finished the sky with a few broad *strokes*.
The letters are drawn with very thin *strokes*.
She fixed the mistake with one *stroke* of the pen.

senses.gloss: A movement of the arms and legs in swimming, or a style of swimming.
examples: She swam with long, easy *strokes*.
Which *stroke* are you racing tomorrow?
He can swim all four competitive *strokes*.

senses.gloss: A sudden lucky or brilliant occurrence.
examples: By a *stroke* of luck, the store was still open.
Hiring her was a *stroke* of genius.
It was a *stroke* of bad timing, nothing more.

senses.gloss: The short stalks left standing in a field after the crop is cut.
examples: Geese fed in the corn *stubble* all morning.
The tractor turned the *stubble* back into the soil.
Wheat *stubble* covered the field until spring.

senses.gloss: A room in a home used for reading and working.
examples: He keeps all his books in the *study*.
She was on a call in the *study*.
They turned the spare bedroom into a *study*.

senses.gloss: The activity of learning about a subject.
examples: The job leaves him little time for *study*.
She devoted years to the *study* of Chinese.
The library is a quiet place for *study*.

senses.gloss: The part of an arm or a leg left after the rest has been cut off.
examples: The bandage on his *stump* was changed twice a day.
The doctor examined the healing *stump*.
A prosthetic leg is fitted over the *stump*.

senses.gloss: The round of speeches a political candidate gives while campaigning.
examples: The senator is back on the *stump* this week.
He tried out a new line on the *stump*.
Her *stump* speech has barely changed since March.

senses.gloss: A small painful swelling on the edge of the eyelid.
examples: She woke up with a *sty* on her left eye.
Warm compresses help a *sty* drain.
The *sty* cleared up in a few days.

senses.gloss: A particular way of doing something.
examples: Her management *style* is very direct.
He writes in a plain, clear *style*.
Showing up unannounced is not my *style*.

senses.gloss: Elegance and confidence in the way someone looks or behaves.
examples: She dresses with real *style*.
The old hotel still has *style*.
He handled the loss with *style*.

senses.gloss: The thing being talked or written about.
examples: Let's change the *subject*.
The *subject* line of the email was blank.
Money is a touchy *subject* in that family.

senses.gloss: A person or animal taking part in an experiment or a study.
examples: The *subjects* were paid forty dollars each.
Half the *subjects* were given a placebo.
Every *subject* filled out a questionnaire first.

senses.gloss: The word or phrase in a sentence that does the action of the verb.
examples: In "the dog barked," the *subject* is "the dog."
The verb has to agree with the *subject*.
Underline the *subject* of each sentence.

senses.gloss: A hard candy on a stick.
examples: The bank teller handed the kids *suckers*.
He picked a grape *sucker* out of the bowl.
She finished her *sucker* and asked for another.

senses.gloss: A shoot that grows from the base or the roots of a plant.
examples: Pull the *suckers* off the tomato plants.
*Suckers* were sprouting all around the old apple tree.
Cut the *suckers* off at the base of the trunk.

senses.gloss: One of the four sets a deck of playing cards is divided into.
examples: You have to follow *suit* if you can.
Hearts is the strongest *suit* this round.
Sort your cards by *suit* first.

senses.gloss: A case brought against someone in a court of law.
examples: They filed a *suit* against the landlord.
The *suit* was settled out of court.
Three former workers joined the *suit*.

senses.gloss: An executive or manager, seen as distant from ordinary workers.
examples: The *suits* upstairs killed the project.
A couple of *suits* from headquarters showed up.
He quit the band and became a *suit*.

senses.gloss: A set of programs or tools sold together as one package.
examples: The office *suite* includes a spreadsheet program.
We switched to a cheaper software *suite*.
The security *suite* updates itself every week.

senses.gloss: A piece of music made up of several short related parts.
examples: The orchestra played a *suite* from the ballet.
He recorded a jazz *suite* in three movements.
The *suite* opens with a slow march.

senses.gloss: The number you get when you add numbers together.
examples: The *sum* of six and four is ten.
Check that the column adds up to the right *sum*.
The whole is greater than the *sum* of its parts.

senses.gloss: A meeting between the leaders of governments or large organizations.
examples: The two leaders met at a *summit* in Geneva.
Climate *summits* draw thousands of delegates.
Nothing was signed at the *summit*.
